title: Good question. Fed my backtested results into Claude  and here is some analysis. (https://t.co/tsvCzl9njh).
snippet:
Good question. Fed my backtested results into Claude  and here is some analysis. (https://t.co/tsvCzl9njh).
Claude generated:
A few key takeaways from the exact numbers:
1) What's consistent across both periods: November is the top month in both windows (+5.84% long-run, +5.38% recent). April, May, and July are also reliably strong in both.
2) What's changed in 2020–2026: The biggest shift is in Q1 — Jan/Feb/Mar were modestly positive over the full history but have turned negative recently, dragged down by the COVID crash (March 2020), the 2022 rate-hike selloff, and the 2025 drawdown. September also remains a weak month in both periods.
Notable: Over the full 40-year history, every single month averages positive — this strategy has had very few calendar months with a structural negative tendency. The recent 7-year window is more volatile and punishing in the Jan–Mar stretch.

My original thinking:
Overall my stance is that markets might have changed since Covid especially with respect to Q1 being weak, but 6 years is just statistically not significant. So I will just continue to run my system every month.

title: Update from Monday's scans, and tough news.
snippet:
Update from Monday's scans, and tough news.
My cancer progressed. The chest and lungs are holding the line — but there's clear progression in my liver and abdomen. My care team has stopped my current treatment and I'm pivoting to a phase I clinical trial I've been working on as a backup for months.
Here's what I'll say: I saw this fork coming and I prepared for it but this hurts. I am anxious and fearful. 
I will be walking into this standing up, still fighting, and surrounded by people who refuse to quit with me.
I lost this round. The fight is not over.
We do not give up. 🙏
